head_commit.message:
PR #50937: [XLA:GPU] Account for tiles per program in Triton launch dimensions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50937

📝 Summary of Changes
Compute triton launch block counts as `ceil(num_tiles / num_tiles_per_pid)`, matching the existing XTile schedule.

🎯 Justification
The launch calculation previously requested one block per output tile, even when the generated kernel assigns multiple tiles to each program. `GetNumberOfBlocks`, assumed one tile per block, it is renamed `GetNumberOfTiles` and the number of block is computed based on it and the `num_tiles_per_pid`.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

🧪 Unit Tests:
Add `LaunchConfigAccountsForTilesPerProgram` in `fusion_test.cc` for 32 output tiles, it checks that 1, 4, and 3 tiles per program produce 32, 8, and 11 blocks
Without the fix, the multi tile cases incorrectly return 32 blocks. With, all tests pass.

Copybara import of the project:

--
63ad2e5b3661aabdd755ef9218ff969f63809d08 by Louis Lechevalier <louis@zml.ai>:

[XLA:GPU] Account for tiles per program in Triton launch dimensions

Count output tiles separately from launch blocks, dividing by tiles per
program to match the existing consecutive tile assignment and bounded loop.
The default one-tile-per-program configuration preserves existing launches.

Add launch-configuration regression coverage for 32 output tiles with one,
four, and three tiles per program, expecting 32, 8, and 11 blocks. Preserve
the existing default-configuration coverage and check that thread counts
remain unchanged.

Merging this change closes #50937

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add GetDefaultCompilationPipeline in gpu_pipeline.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add GetDefaultCompilationPipeline in gpu_pipeline.

This change adds the gpu_pipeline library with GetDefaultCompilationPipeline.
The function returns the HLO pass pipeline of the GPU compiler as an
HloPipelineProto. For now, the proto has two sub-pipelines,
"annotate-host-compute" and "pre-spmd-partitioner". They have the same passes
and options as the first two pipelines of OptimizeHloModule.

OptimizeHloModule builds the proto and logs it at VLOG(1). It does not run
the proto yet. OptimizeHloModule still runs the passes with HloPassPipeline.

A new test creates each pass of the default pipeline from the pass registry.
The test makes sure that all pass names are registered and that each pass
reads all of its options. The test does not need a GPU.

The new gpu_pipeline_passes library links the HloPassRegistry registrations of
the passes in the pipeline. Only the test depends on it for now.

display_title: Pre-reserve containers in HloComputation::MakeInstructionPostOrderFrom.

head_commit.message:
Pre-reserve containers in HloComputation::MakeInstructionPostOrderFrom.

Pre-reserve `post_order` and `dfs_stack_scratch` to `instruction_count()` in `HloComputation::MakeInstructionPostOrderFrom` (`xla/hlo/ir/hlo_computation.cc`), matching `HloComputation::MakeInstructionPostOrder` and avoiding repeated `std::vector` reallocations during post-order DFS traversal from a root instruction (such as in `HloCSE::RunOnComputation`).

Microbenchmark results (`--benchmark_repetitions=9`, `-c opt`):

| Benchmark | Baseline | Optimized | Delta |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `BM_MakeInstructionPostOrderFrom/16` | 1,239 ns | 521 ns | -57.9% (2.38x) |
| `BM_MakeInstructionPostOrderFrom/1024` | 18,294 ns | 15,854 ns | -13.3% (1.15x) |

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004710377

display_title: PR #51672: [XLA:GPU] Do not async-wrap instructions for which no thunks are emitted

head_commit.message:
PR #51672: [XLA:GPU] Do not async-wrap instructions for which no thunks are emitted

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51672

📝 Summary of Changes

ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper wrapped every instruction carrying `_xla_stream_annotation` in an async call on the annotated stream, including get-tuple-elements, tuples and bitcasts that inherited the annotation of the op whose results they pick out or rearrange.

Factor the thunk emitter's rule for which instructions emit no thunks out into EmitsNoThunks, use it in the emitter, and make the wrapper drop the annotation from those instructions instead of wrapping them. Instructions that do any device work, however small (e.g. partition-id and replica-id, which write their result with a memset), are still wrapped, so dropping the annotation never moves work to another stream.

🎯 Justification

Such async calls do no work but add synchronization points on the annotated stream and occupy async-compute slots in the latency hiding scheduler.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

🧪 Unit Tests:

Added

🧪 Execution Tests:

n/a

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Pass free_visitors to DeviceAddressVmmAllocator.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Pass free_visitors to DeviceAddressVmmAllocator.

`GpuAllocatorConfig::sub_allocator_free_visitors` was previously only wired into `CreateBFCAllocator`, leaving `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator` (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`) without free callbacks when virtual address ranges are unmapped.

Add `FreeVisitor` support to `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator` (and its CUDA and ROCm subclasses and factories) so registered callbacks are invoked in reverse order immediately before mapped virtual address ranges are unmapped during pending deallocation completion or allocator teardown, and forward `allocator_config.sub_allocator_free_visitors` from `GetStreamExecutorGpuDeviceAllocator`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010384831

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Skip per-command NVTX annotations during in-place command buffer updates.

head_commit.message:
Skip per-command NVTX annotations during in-place command buffer updates.

`CommandExecutor::RecordUpdate` skips `cuGraphExec*NodeSetParams` for commands with unchanged buffer allocations, leaving update-time NVTX attribution in `nsys-ui` (`CUPTI_CBID_RESOURCE_GRAPHNODE_SET_PARAMS`) incomplete and absent from SQLite `CUDA_GRAPH_NODE_EVENTS` while emitting redundant host NVTX ranges every step. Late-start (`cudaProfilerStart`) node profiling requires `--cuda-graph-trace=node:nvtx-precapture` to attribute all nodes from `RecordCreate` without buffering per-step update ranges during warmup.

Remove the outer `ScopedAnnotation` from `CommandExecutor::RecordUpdate` and push it on `RecordUpdate` in commands that rebuild a child graph (`TracedCommand::RecordTracedCommand`, `CollectiveThunk::Record`, `CollectiveGroupThunk::Record`, `RaggedAllToAllThunk::Record`, `CollectiveKernelThunk::Record`, and `HostExecuteStartThunk::Record`) to preserve child-graph re-trace attribution.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010379893

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Lower unfused kScaledDot to cuDNN after GemmFusion.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Lower unfused kScaledDot to cuDNN after GemmFusion.

Problem:    kScaledDot reaches cuDNN only by changing __triton_gemm in place.
Solution:   Run CudnnScaledDotRewriter after GemmFusion.

Keep kScaledDot through layout assignment when cuDNN supports its types.
Wrap it into __triton_gemm only when Triton supports it. After GemmFusion,
CudnnScaledDotRewriter emits a __cudnn$fusion with inline scale swizzle, and
ScaledDotRewriter decomposes the rest for cuBLASLt. CudnnBackend accepts
kScaledDot only in __cudnn$fusion and no longer adds the scale swizzle in
ApplyConfig. Fission backends skip __cudnn$fusion scaled dots, because their
scales are already swizzled.

display_title: Log load time of serialized executables in HLO runner

head_commit.message:
Log load time of serialized executables in HLO runner

When running with --input_format=serialized_pjrt_executable, the time to load the executable was not logged anywhere. This adds an XLA_SCOPED_LOGGING_TIMER around the PjRtClient::LoadSerializedExecutable call in FunctionalHloRunner (and nothing else), so benchmark infrastructure can track AOT load time the same way it tracks ExecuteOnDevices.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Pass free_visitors to DeviceAddressVmmAllocator.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Pass free_visitors to DeviceAddressVmmAllocator.

`GpuAllocatorConfig::sub_allocator_free_visitors` was previously only wired into `CreateBFCAllocator`, leaving `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator` (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`) without free callbacks when virtual address ranges are unmapped.

Add `FreeVisitor` support to `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator` (and its CUDA and ROCm subclasses and factories) so registered callbacks are invoked in reverse order immediately before mapped virtual address ranges are unmapped during pending deallocation completion or allocator teardown, and forward `allocator_config.sub_allocator_free_visitors` from `GetStreamExecutorGpuDeviceAllocator`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010289448

display_title: PR #50406: [GPU] Preserve memory-space annotations in dynamic-slice fusions

head_commit.message:
PR #50406: [GPU] Preserve memory-space annotations in dynamic-slice fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50406

This fixes a case where dynamic-slice fusion can leave an FFI call’s buffers in ordinary memory even though the call requests collective (symmetric) memory, `S(7)`.

Consider this structure, with a 128-element `input` and 256-element `weights` and `destination` buffers. These are schematic HLO excerpts; the attribute names and indices are exact:

```text
tile = slice(weights, [128:256])
tmp = custom_call(input, tile),
      frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{0:7}",
                           results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
out = dynamic_update_slice(destination, tmp, 128)
```

The call requests collective memory for `input` and its result. Fusion replaces the temporary slices with views into their backing buffers:

```text
fused(p0_weights, p1_input, p2_destination) {
  tile = slice(p0_weights, [128:256])
  tmp = custom_call(p1_input, tile),
        frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{0:7}",
                             results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
  return dynamic_update_slice(p2_destination, tmp, 128)
}
```

Previously, the requirements remained only on the inner call, where allocation and boundary-copy analysis could miss them:

```text
out = fusion(weights, input, destination), calls=fused
```

This change puts the corresponding requirements on the outer fusion:

```text
out = fusion(weights, input, destination), calls=fused,
      frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{1:7,2:7}",
                           results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
```

The call’s operand `0` becomes fusion operand `1`. The destination at operand `2` also needs collective memory because the FFI now writes directly into its slice. `weights` stays in ordinary memory. Entry-boundary copies preserve ordinary-memory inputs and outputs where required.

The rewrite also preserves explicit input/output aliases. For example:

```text
tile = dynamic_slice(x, i)
updated = custom_call(tile, y)  // result aliases operand 0
out = dynamic_update_slice(x, updated, i)
```

This in-place update can fuse when the existing buffer and offset analysis proves that the aliased input and output refer to the same backing buffer and byte range. Mismatched regions, additional accesses sharing that backing buffer, or memory-space requirements that would conflict after fusion leave the call unfused.

Annotation handling is limited to custom calls and the `dynamic_slice_fusion` subtype.

Regression coverage includes operand reindexing, tuple outputs, update destinations, conflicting requests, O2 rollback, matching in-place updates, rejected overlaps, and shared collective allocation.
Copybara import of the project:

--
5ad0c53e46b3c8e34c1fb886b90a6b3059537f37 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Preserve memory-space annotations in dynamic-slice fusions

Remap custom-call memory requirements to the fusion buffers that collective copy insertion and buffer assignment see. Preserve compatible slice fusions while declining merges that require conflicting memory spaces.

--
bbeb8973d395276434b991b02746b25064329191 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Isolate the extended-offset annotation regression

Provide static slice configs directly so the regression exercises memory-space propagation while the fusion candidate is detached from its module.

--
7f32bc9803d43f81ae014d334c26029faedd950b by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Limit fusion memory annotations to dynamic-slice wrappers

Other fusion passes may inherit index-based frontend annotations without remapping their operands. Restrict buffer coloring and collective boundary-copy insertion to custom calls and recognized dynamic-slice fusions, with regressions for unrelated fusion kinds.

--
58e8f9ac2371e548f49f811ccdafc0896e99fa3c by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Preserve custom-call aliases across dynamic-slice fusion

Decline fusion when a captured slice or update changes an explicitly aliased custom-call buffer. Keep directly inferred aliases and cover shared collective allocation, tuple outputs, and operand restoration after rejected O2 rewrites.

--
ddc922ec7e3387414e139bbf628c62c84d6adf53 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Allow matching aliased slice updates in dynamic-slice fusion

Use existing buffer mappings and offset configurations to preserve custom-call aliases when a slice is updated in place. Reject mismatched regions and additional accesses to the same backing buffer, and cover accepted fusion plus shared collective allocation.

--
bb4e31fbb3d80dd9d7dee12d0331b4ffc60ed81f by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Preserve frontend attributes when remapping fusion memory spaces

Apply remapped memory spaces after instruction replacement so unrelated frontend attributes retain their existing inheritance behavior. Remove inherited memory-space maps before merging to avoid stale indices, including when the remap is empty.

Cover direct custom-call replacement, DUS attribute precedence, empty memory-space maps, and tuple-result attribute preservation.

--
a85a4aecbfb2ba1c59adbe6c246c65838a4da580 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Encapsulate replacement of memory-space attributes

Move selective memory-space attribute replacement into a local helper so clearing stale indices and preserving unrelated attributes stay together. Keep the call after instruction replacement to preserve attribute inheritance.

--
0836b5db643c0882b640008c4d85d2a26d50d530 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[HLO] Add frontend attribute update and replacement utilities

Provide explicit attribute overrides and removals while retaining unrelated keys. Add opt-in instruction replacement that merges inherited attributes even when replacement attributes are already set, retaining replacement values and the operand-forwarding guard.

Use these utilities in dynamic-slice fusion so additional attributes cannot suppress inheritance. Cover precedence, removal, self-referencing updates, forwarding, and declined replacement in focused unit tests.

--
38f519801763fd420dd53309ab08ba6d1ae72460 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Decline slice fusion for out-of-range memory-space indices

Log and skip fusion when an operand or result memory-space annotation cannot be remapped. Preserve the original call instead of introducing a compilation error in an optional optimization; downstream assignment currently ignores unmatched indices.

Cover negative and upper-bound indices for both annotations, including rollback of O2 operand rewrites and discarded partial mappings.

--
891107553136f133a90cf183078b5711a659b774 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[HLO] Match CI include ordering in instruction utility tests

--
43ae994e11d594ce57ee3399d3a2dda3de62e5ce by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Restore errors for invalid memory-space annotation indices

Reject out-of-range operand and result indices during fusion remapping because downstream assignment ignores unmatched indices instead of reporting an error. Update the regression to require InvalidArgument for negative and upper-bound indices.

--
abb184379bf11d5e50de4090c442422ef89feac8 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Test copy separation for aliased slice fusion inputs

--
52a43361ce57f3975ceabb50942c123f32760cef by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Simplify dynamic-slice fusion replacement and rollback

Use standard instruction replacement to preserve frontend attributes without a redundant public helper. Reject control-dependent outputs before replacement, keep operand rollback within fusion rewriting, and make memory-space annotation support checks private.

--
a3c0d70caaa5298f28744263d635916ecf39bbc6 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Preserve memory spaces through dynamic-slice alias copies

Allow fusion when aliased inputs and outputs use separate buffers, and propagate operand memory requirements to the runtime copy destination. Keep conflicting updates outside the fusion to preserve other input reads.

Add regression coverage for separate buffers, overlapping accesses, and conflicting annotations. Targeted Bazel tests were blocked before compilation by DNS failures fetching CUDA dependencies.

--
bfdf829c1dd7c2be6c78ac47c32a38016b95a783 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Check dynamic-slice fusion output memory-space layouts

Skip fusion when a mapped result annotation conflicts with its output layout, using the same compatibility check as operands. Cover array and tuple results with default, matching, legacy collective, and conflicting memory spaces.

Targeted tests remain unverified: Bazel was stopped before compilation after CUDA dependency fetching stalled.

--
567d6e7665b3cb4e7455dff5876179461405d188 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Skip dynamic-slice fusion with result control dependencies

Allow valid HLO with result control dependencies to continue without fusion. Check before planning or cloning, and verify that skipping preserves the module.

Adapt memory-space predicate coverage to main, where the buffer-analysis helper is now private.

--
de2aecc44bb2890ceaaeb3a6f80f666c041fd6f7 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Fix lint for dynamic-slice memory-space tests

Reuse the indexed color lookup to preserve tuple-result assertions without adding deprecated color calls. Declare the test layout dependency and retain the HLO sharding implementation dependency.

Merging this change closes #50406

head_commit.message:
[Pallas:TPU] Zero-extend 16-bit argmax/argmin indices to int32

tpu.reduce_index on bf16 inputs produces 16-bit indices, and the reduced
dimension may have up to 2^16 elements, so the indices must be interpreted as

head_commit.message:
PR #51905: [XLA:GPU] Forward FFI RECORD handlers through PJRT registration

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51905

### Summary of Changes

Forward the optional FFI RECORD handler through GPU PJRT custom-call registration. GPU extension v4 appends the handler and a runtime capability flag; structure-size checks preserve compatibility with older callers.

### Justification

XLA supports RECORD, but the GPU PJRT registration interface currently carries only instantiate, prepare, initialize, and execute. A JAX GPU registration containing a `record` callback therefore never reaches XLA's RECORD path. This provides the interface needed by the companion JAX change and lets clients detect unsupported plugins before registering.

This change only exposes registration; it does not change graph invalidation or replay behavior.

### Kind of Contribution

Bug fix; tests.

### Validation

Added registry tests for forwarding the RECORD callback, advertising support, and ignoring the appended field when an older argument size is supplied. Existing test argument structures are zero-initialized to cover the added optional field.

C11 and C++17 public-header compilation passed. GPU registry tests have not been run locally because the development host is macOS without CUDA. The focused command for Linux/CUDA is:

```sh
bazel test --config=cuda //xla/pjrt/c:pjrt_c_api_gpu_test_nvgpu_any \
  --test_filter='PjrtCApiGpuExtensionTest.CustomCall*' --test_output=errors
```

head_commit.message:
PR #50406: [GPU] Preserve memory-space annotations in dynamic-slice fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50406

This fixes a case where dynamic-slice fusion can leave an FFI call’s buffers in ordinary memory even though the call requests collective (symmetric) memory, `S(7)`.

Consider this structure, with a 128-element `input` and 256-element `weights` and `destination` buffers. These are schematic HLO excerpts; the attribute names and indices are exact:

```text
tile = slice(weights, [128:256])
tmp = custom_call(input, tile),
      frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{0:7}",
                           results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
out = dynamic_update_slice(destination, tmp, 128)
```

The call requests collective memory for `input` and its result. Fusion replaces the temporary slices with views into their backing buffers:

```text
fused(p0_weights, p1_input, p2_destination) {
  tile = slice(p0_weights, [128:256])
  tmp = custom_call(p1_input, tile),
        frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{0:7}",
                             results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
  return dynamic_update_slice(p2_destination, tmp, 128)
}
```

Previously, the requirements remained only on the inner call, where allocation and boundary-copy analysis could miss them:

```text
out = fusion(weights, input, destination), calls=fused
```

This change puts the corresponding requirements on the outer fusion:

```text
out = fusion(weights, input, destination), calls=fused,
      frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{1:7,2:7}",
                           results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
```

The call’s operand `0` becomes fusion operand `1`. The destination at operand `2` also needs collective memory because the FFI now writes directly into its slice. `weights` stays in ordinary memory. Entry-boundary copies preserve ordinary-memory inputs and outputs where required.

The rewrite also preserves explicit input/output aliases. For example:

```text
tile = dynamic_slice(x, i)
updated = custom_call(tile, y)  // result aliases operand 0
out = dynamic_update_slice(x, updated, i)
```

This in-place update can fuse when the existing buffer and offset analysis proves that the aliased input and output refer to the same backing buffer and byte range. Mismatched regions, additional accesses sharing that backing buffer, or memory-space requirements that would conflict after fusion leave the call unfused.

Annotation handling is limited to custom calls and the `dynamic_slice_fusion` subtype.

Regression coverage includes operand reindexing, tuple outputs, update destinations, conflicting requests, O2 rollback, matching in-place updates, rejected overlaps, and shared collective allocation.

bbeb8973d395276434b991b02746b25064329191 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Isolate the extended-offset annotation regression

Provide static slice configs directly so the regression exercises memory-space propagation while the fusion candidate is detached from its module.

[GPU] Limit fusion memory annotations to dynamic-slice wrappers

Other fusion passes may inherit index-based frontend annotations without remapping their operands. Restrict buffer coloring and collective boundary-copy insertion to custom calls and recognized dynamic-slice fusions, with regressions for unrelated fusion kinds.

58e8f9ac2371e548f49f811ccdafc0896e99fa3c by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Preserve custom-call aliases across dynamic-slice fusion

Decline fusion when a captured slice or update changes an explicitly aliased custom-call buffer. Keep directly inferred aliases and cover shared collective allocation, tuple outputs, and operand restoration after rejected O2 rewrites.

[HLO] Match CI include ordering in instruction utility tests

abb184379bf11d5e50de4090c442422ef89feac8 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Test copy separation for aliased slice fusion inputs

--
52a43361ce57f3975ceabb50942c123f32760cef by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Simplify dynamic-slice fusion replacement and rollback

Use standard instruction replacement to preserve frontend attributes without a redundant public helper. Reject control-dependent outputs before replacement, keep operand rollback within fusion rewriting, and make memory-space annotation support checks private.

--
a3c0d70caaa5298f28744263d635916ecf39bbc6 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Preserve memory spaces through dynamic-slice alias copies

Allow fusion when aliased inputs and outputs use separate buffers, and propagate operand memory requirements to the runtime copy destination. Keep conflicting updates outside the fusion to preserve other input reads.

Add regression coverage for separate buffers, overlapping accesses, and conflicting annotations. Targeted Bazel tests were blocked before compilation by DNS failures fetching CUDA dependencies.

--
bfdf829c1dd7c2be6c78ac47c32a38016b95a783 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Check dynamic-slice fusion output memory-space layouts

Skip fusion when a mapped result annotation conflicts with its output layout, using the same compatibility check as operands. Cover array and tuple results with default, matching, legacy collective, and conflicting memory spaces.

Targeted tests remain unverified: Bazel was stopped before compilation after CUDA dependency fetching stalled.

--
567d6e7665b3cb4e7455dff5876179461405d188 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Skip dynamic-slice fusion with result control dependencies

Allow valid HLO with result control dependencies to continue without fusion. Check before planning or cloning, and verify that skipping preserves the module.

Adapt memory-space predicate coverage to main, where the buffer-analysis helper is now private.

--
de2aecc44bb2890ceaaeb3a6f80f666c041fd6f7 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[GPU] Fix lint for dynamic-slice memory-space tests

Reuse the indexed color lookup to preserve tuple-result assertions without adding deprecated color calls. Declare the test layout dependency and retain the HLO sharding implementation dependency.

Merging this change closes #50406

head_commit.message:
PR #45999: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Emitter: kRaggedBatch mode (PR 5/8)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45999

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR is the fifth in a series of eight aiming to enable the Triton backend for the `ragged-dot` operation using triton group-gemm kernels, based on the experimental tiling strategy.

PR 1/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45995
PR 2/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45996
PR 3/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45997
PR 4/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45998
PR 5/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45999   <---- This PR
PR 6/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46000
PR 7/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46001
PR 8/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46002

This PR adds the kRaggedBatch implementation in EmitRaggedDot().
kRaggedBatch is a regular batched GEMM where group_sizes control scheduling only (not computation): output[b,:,:] = LHS[b,:,:] @ RHS[b,:,:] for all b in [0, B_total).

🎯 Justification
The default way for handling ragged-dot ops is to expand the ragged-dot matrix into zero-padded matrices then rewriting the ragged-dot into a batched dot between the padded matrices and the second operand, which results in numerous unnecessary calculations.
Although there are other, more efficient backends (CuDNN and Hipblast), these are not capable of handling all possible configurations.
In this context, having another, more generic Triton backend could enable good performance for ‘ragged-dot’ operations on all targets and for all input configurations.
The order in which backends are selected is as follows:
1. Cudnn if compatible Cuda target or Hipblaslt if compatible HIP target
2. Triton backend if compatible input configuration
3. Default rewriting

head_commit.message:
PR #51905: [XLA:GPU] Forward FFI RECORD handlers through PJRT registration

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51905

### Summary of Changes

Forward the optional FFI RECORD handler through GPU PJRT custom-call registration. GPU extension v4 appends the handler and a runtime capability flag; structure-size checks preserve compatibility with older callers.

### Justification

XLA supports RECORD, but the GPU PJRT registration interface currently carries only instantiate, prepare, initialize, and execute. A JAX GPU registration containing a `record` callback therefore never reaches XLA's RECORD path. This provides the interface needed by the companion JAX change and lets clients detect unsupported plugins before registering.

This change only exposes registration; it does not change graph invalidation or replay behavior.

### Kind of Contribution

Bug fix; tests.

### Validation

Added registry tests for forwarding the RECORD callback, advertising support, and ignoring the appended field when an older argument size is supplied. Existing test argument structures are zero-initialized to cover the added optional field.

C11 and C++17 public-header compilation passed. GPU registry tests have not been run locally because the development host is macOS without CUDA. The focused command for Linux/CUDA is:

```sh
bazel test --config=cuda //xla/pjrt/c:pjrt_c_api_gpu_test_nvgpu_any \
  --test_filter='PjrtCApiGpuExtensionTest.CustomCall*' --test_output=errors
```

head_commit.message:
PR #51846: [XLA:GPU] Avoid double-rounding F64 -> F8/F4 conversions through F32 in ConvertFloatNvidiaPass

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51846

#ai-generated

## Status quo

On NVIDIA GPUs where `ConvertFloatNvidiaPass` is enabled (`(ptx >= 78 && cc >= 90) || (ptx >= 81 && cc >= 89)` for `f8E4M3FN` and `f8E5M2`, and `ptx >= 86 && cc >= 100` for `f4E2M1FN`), `RewriteTruncFPattern` in `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms/convert_float_nvidia.cc` rewrites every `arith.truncf` to `f8E4M3FN`, `f8E5M2`, or `f4E2M1FN` by first converting any non-`f16` source to `f32` via `ConvertToF32` (`arith.truncf ... : f64 to f32`) and then emitting the NVVM `f32 -> f8/f4` conversion intrinsic (`cvt.rn.f32.f64` followed by `cvt.rn.satfinite.e4m3x2.f32` / `e5m2x2.f32` / `e2m1x2.f32`). The overflow fix-up (`FixInfinityConversionValue`) also tests the `f32`-rounded value.

## Why

Because every rounding midpoint of `f8E4M3FN`, `f8E5M2`, and `f4E2M1FN` (and the overflow thresholds of `f8E4M3FN` and `f8E5M2`) is an exact `f32` value with an even significand, `f64` inputs that lie within half an `f32` ulp past an `f8`/`f4` midpoint or threshold are first rounded onto the midpoint in `f32` and then rounded the wrong way by the second tie-to-even step (compare `openxla/xla#42731`, which fixed the analogous `f64/f32 -> f16 -> f8` double rounding on `XLA:CPU`):

| `float64` input | Target | `XLA:GPU` (`sm_90`) before | Correctly rounded (`XLA:CPU`, HLO constant folder) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `1 + 2^-4 + 2^-30` | `f8e4m3fn` | `1.0` | `1.125` |
| `464 + 2^-20` | `f8e4m3fn` | `448.0` | `NaN` (overflow) |
| `2^-10 + 2^-40` | `f8e4m3fn` | `0.0` | `0.001953125` (`2^-9`) |
| `1 + 2^-3 + 2^-30` | `f8e5m2` | `1.0` | `1.25` |
| `61440 - 2^-10` | `f8e5m2` | `inf` | `57344.0` |
| `2^-17 + 2^-47` | `f8e5m2` | `0.0` | `1.52587890625e-05` (`2^-16`) |

## Design choices

PTX has no direct `f64 -> f8/f4` instruction. In `RewriteTruncFPattern::matchAndRewrite`, return `notifyMatchFailure` when `src.getType().getWidth() > 32` so that `f64 -> f8/f4` truncations are lowered by the subsequent `ExpandFloatOpsPass` (`EmitFloatConversion`, which converts directly from the `f64` bits in a single rounding, as already used for the other 8-bit float types and on GPUs below `sm_89`). Update `@intr_f64_to_f8` in `convert_float_nvidia.mlir` accordingly.

- On `f64` NaN inputs, `ExpandFloatOpsPass` preserves the NaN sign bit (`0x7f`/`0xff` for `e4m3fn`, `0x7e`/`0xfe` for `e5m2`), matching `XLA:CPU` bit-for-bit, whereas the `f32`/`f16`/`bf16` hardware intrinsic path continues to emit the unsigned NaN `0x7f` for both formats.
- `f64 -> f4E2M1FN` on `sm_100+` is covered by the same `getWidth() > 32` guard (verified at the MLIR level with `emitters_opt`).

## Trade-offs / Alternatives

- **Trade-offs:** `f64 -> f8/f4` conversions now use `ExpandFloatOpsPass`'s bit-manipulation lowering instead of the `f32` hardware conversion intrinsic. All `f32`, `f16`, and `bf16` conversions to `f8`/`f4` continue to use the hardware intrinsic path unchanged.
- **Alternatives:** Narrowing `f64 -> f32` with round-to-odd (sticky-bit preservation) before the `f32 -> f8/f4` hardware intrinsic would avoid double rounding while keeping the intrinsic, but PTX `cvt` has no round-to-odd mode for `f64 -> f32`, so it would require custom integer bit manipulation prior to the intrinsic anyway instead of reusing `ExpandFloatOpsPass`.

## Reproducer (JAX on `sm_90`)

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)

x_e4 = jnp.array([1.0 + 2**-4 + 2**-30, 464.0 + 2**-20, 2**-10 + 2**-40], dtype=jnp.float64)
x_e5 = jnp.array([1.0 + 2**-3 + 2**-30, 61440.0 - 2**-10, 2**-17 + 2**-47], dtype=jnp.float64)

print("e4m3fn GPU:", jax.jit(lambda x: x.astype(jnp.float8_e4m3fn))(x_e4).astype(jnp.float32))
# Before: [  1. 448.   0.]
# After:  [1.125             nan 0.00195312]

print("e5m2   GPU:", jax.jit(lambda x: x.astype(jnp.float8_e5m2))(x_e5).astype(jnp.float32))
# Before: [ 1. inf  0.]
# After:  [1.2500000e+00 5.7344000e+04 1.5258789e-05]
```

## Tests

- `bazel test //xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms/tests:all //xla/codegen/emitters/transforms/tests:all //xla/backends/gpu/tests:float_conversions_test_h100 //xla/tests:convert_test_h100` (36/36 targets, 534 test cases passed on H100).

display_title: Let backends ignore the layout constraints of custom calls

head_commit.message:
Let backends ignore the layout constraints of custom calls

Adds LayoutAssignment::IgnoreCustomCallLayoutConstraints. A backend returns
true for a custom call that does not depend on the layouts of its operands
and results. Layout assignment then neither constrains its operands nor
copies its aliased operands, and afterwards sets its
operand_shapes_with_layout to the assigned layouts. The default is false, so
no backend changes behavior.

In `RewriteTruncFPattern::matchAndRewrite`, return `notifyMatchFailure` when `src.getType().getWidth() > 32` so that `f64 -> f8/f4` truncations are lowered by the subsequent `ExpandFloatOpsPass` (`EmitFloatConversion`, which converts directly from the `f64` bits in a single rounding, as already used for the other 8-bit float types and on GPUs below `sm_89`). Update `@intr_f64_to_f8` in `convert_float_nvidia.mlir` accordingly.

- On `f64` NaN inputs, `ExpandFloatOpsPass` preserves the NaN sign bit (`0x7f`/`0xff` for `e4m3fn`, `0x7e`/`0xfe` for `e5m2`), matching `XLA:CPU` bit-for-bit, whereas the `f32`/`f16`/`bf16` hardware intrinsic path continues to emit the unsigned NaN `0x7f` for both formats.
- `f64 -> f4E2M1FN` on `sm_100+` is covered by the same `getWidth() > 32` guard (verified at the MLIR level with `emitters_opt`).

## Trade-offs / Alternatives

- **Trade-offs:** `f64 -> f8/f4` conversions now use `ExpandFloatOpsPass`'s bit-manipulation lowering instead of the `f32` hardware conversion intrinsic. All `f32`, `f16`, and `bf16` conversions to `f8`/`f4` continue to use the hardware intrinsic path unchanged.
- **Alternatives:** Narrowing `f64 -> f32` with round-to-odd (sticky-bit preservation) before the `f32 -> f8/f4` hardware intrinsic would avoid double rounding while keeping the intrinsic, but PTX `cvt` has no round-to-odd mode for `f64 -> f32`, so it would require custom integer bit manipulation prior to the intrinsic anyway instead of reusing `ExpandFloatOpsPass`.

## Reproducer (JAX on `sm_90`)

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)

x_e4 = jnp.array([1.0 + 2**-4 + 2**-30, 464.0 + 2**-20, 2**-10 + 2**-40], dtype=jnp.float64)
x_e5 = jnp.array([1.0 + 2**-3 + 2**-30, 61440.0 - 2**-10, 2**-17 + 2**-47], dtype=jnp.float64)

print("e4m3fn GPU:", jax.jit(lambda x: x.astype(jnp.float8_e4m3fn))(x_e4).astype(jnp.float32))
# Before: [  1. 448.   0.]
# After:  [1.125             nan 0.00195312]

print("e5m2   GPU:", jax.jit(lambda x: x.astype(jnp.float8_e5m2))(x_e5).astype(jnp.float32))
# Before: [ 1. inf  0.]
# After:  [1.2500000e+00 5.7344000e+04 1.5258789e-05]
```

display_title: Switch from libstdc++ to statically linked libc++

head_commit.message:
Switch from libstdc++ to statically linked libc++

This update enables building and testing Tensorflow with statically linked libc++ (LLVM 22) on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), adds C++20 support, and introduces Manylinux 2.27 compatible wheels.

Patches:
third_party/tensorflow/third_party/tf_runtime/invoke_result.patch
Replaces std::result_of_t (removed in C++20 libc++) with std::invoke_result_t in @tf_runtime, which is pinned to an external GitHub commit in OSS builds.

third_party/xla/third_party/mkl_dnn/eltwise_injector_lower_bound.patch
Why needed: Replaces entry_map_.find(key) on std::multimap with entry_map_.lower_bound(key) in @onednn_async (v3.12.3), @onednn_async_aarch64, and @mkl_dnn_acl_compatible (v3.11.3) so eltwise_injector iterates over all matching entries under C++20 libc++ (fixing the segfault in //tensorflow/core/kernels/mkl:mkl_fused_ops_test).

third_party/tensorflow/third_party/com_google_highway/build.patch
Why needed: Updates hunk context lines for the com_google_highway bump from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0.

Other changes
third_party/tensorflow/core/kernels/cwise_ops.h
In libc++, std::function has a different size and alignment on the x86_64 host (sizeof = 48, alignof = 16 due to 16-byte long double alignment in std::aligned_storage) than on the NVPTX64 CUDA device (sizeof = 32, alignof = 8). Because the comparison functors in cwise_ops.h inherited from std::function<bool(T, T)> and are embedded by value inside Eigen::TensorEvaluator CUDA kernel arguments, this host/device layout mismatch shifted the offsets of the GPU tensor pointers in the kernel parameter buffer and caused CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS crashes. Replacing : std::function<bool(T, T)> with using result_type = bool; keeps the typedef required by Eigen while making the functors stateless 1-byte structs with identical layout on host and device.

third_party/tensorflow/core/util/gpu_device_functions.h
In CUDA device code, Eigen::half (__half) and Eigen::bfloat16 (__nv_bfloat16) have explicit Eigen::numext::bit_cast specializations to and from uint16_t (using CUDA intrinsics like __half_as_ushort and __ushort_as_bfloat16), but no direct specialization between Eigen::half and Eigen::bfloat16. Without a direct specialization, Eigen::numext::bit_cast<Eigen::bfloat16>(Eigen::half) falls back to memcpy between two different class types in device registers, which NVCC's device compiler (cicc) optimizes into 0—causing GpuAtomicAdd on bfloat16 (e.g., in gather_op_test_gpu) to produce all zeros. Routing the conversion through uint16_t in detail::GpuAtomicCasHelper uses the explicit CUDA intrinsic specializations instead of the broken memcpy fallback.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add unit tests for async barrier `output_to_operand_aliasing` usage

Add unit tests in `hlo_alias_analysis_test` covering TensorCore and SparseCore
async barrier `all-to-all` HLO graphs.
1. Verify that all 3 buffers allocated by the barrier start operation alias the
   corresponding `async-start` and `async-done` buffers.
2. Verify that their `HloLiveRange` lifecycles extend to or past `async-done`.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/analysis:hlo_alias_analysis_test`: verifies `HloBuffer` identity
  and `HloLiveRange` end times across `async-start` and `async-done` for both
  TensorCore and SparseCore async barrier patterns.

head_commit.message:
[SDY][Performance] Replicate indivisible scan-dim sharding when a divisible non-scan dim exists for mhlo.scan.

When an `mhlo.scan` is sharded along a scan dimension whose size is not divisible by the shard count and an unsharded divisible non-scan dimension exists, return `std::nullopt` in `ScanPartitioningOpInterface::resolvePermutationFactors` to fall back to replicating the scan dimension and running a single scan rather than a 3-phase prefix scan with padding shifts.

In CUDA device code, Eigen::half (__half) and Eigen::bfloat16 (__nv_bfloat16) have explicit Eigen::numext::bit_cast specializations to and from uint16_t (using CUDA intrinsics like __half_as_ushort and __ushort_as_bfloat16), but no direct specialization between Eigen::half and Eigen::bfloat16. Without a direct specialization, Eigen::numext::bit_cast<Eigen::bfloat16>(Eigen::half) falls back to memcpy between two different class types in device registers, which NVCC's device compiler (cicc) optimizes into 0—causing GpuAtomicAdd on bfloat16 (e.g., in gather_op_test_gpu) to produce all zeros. Routing the conversion through uint16_t in detail::GpuAtomicCasHelper uses the explicit CUDA intrinsic specializations instead of the broken memcpy fallback.

head_commit.message:
Skip per-command NVTX annotations during in-place command buffer updates.

`CommandExecutor::RecordUpdate` skips `cuGraphExec*NodeSetParams` for commands with unchanged buffer allocations, leaving update-time NVTX attribution in `nsys-ui` (`CUPTI_CBID_RESOURCE_GRAPHNODE_SET_PARAMS`) incomplete and absent from SQLite `CUDA_GRAPH_NODE_EVENTS` while emitting redundant host NVTX ranges every step. name: CI ROCm
display_title: Add post-scheduling control dependencies to async callers in CopyRemover.

head_commit.message:
Add post-scheduling control dependencies to async callers in CopyRemover.

When `CopyRemover::TryElideCopy` runs with `insert_post_scheduling_control_dependencies=true`, `LiveRangeBefore` (via `HloOrdering::UsesBeforeValueDefinition`) resolves instructions inside an async wrapped computation (`IsAsyncComputation()`) to their `kAsyncStart` caller in the parent computation when checking whether uses of `src` execute before the definition of `dst`. However, `AddControlDependenciesBetween` previously checked `use->instruction->parent() != dst->value->instruction()->parent()` directly on the inner async computation instruction and skipped adding the control dependency whenever `src` or `dst` lived inside an async computation.

Without that control dependency from the last use of `src` to the `kAsyncStart` caller of `dst`, later passes such as `HloRematerialization` could rematerialize a reader of `src` after `kAsyncStart` / `kAsyncDone` had already overwritten the shared buffer.

Resolve instructions in async computations to their `kAsyncStart` caller in `AddControlDependenciesBetween`, and verify `ordering_->ExecutesBefore(use_inst, dst_inst)` so that in-place async operations (where `src->uses` includes the `kAsyncDone` / `kAsyncUpdate` instruction) do not add a backward control edge to `kAsyncStart`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Restrict hwloc topology discovery in `numa_hwloc.cc` to NUMA and CPU objects.

head_commit.message:
Restrict hwloc topology discovery in `numa_hwloc.cc` to NUMA and CPU objects.

By default, `GetHWLocTopology()` in `numa_hwloc.cc` loads the full machine hardware hierarchy—including CPU cache levels, PCI/OS I/O devices (`linuxio`), and per-core `x86` CPUID probing—even though TSL's NUMA utilities only ever query `HWLOC_OBJ_NUMANODE` and CPU affinity sets. On large multi-socket / high-core-count hosts, this redundant discovery adds unnecessary sysfs traversal and CPUID probing overhead during NUMA initialization. This change configures `HWLOC_TYPE_FILTER_KEEP_NONE` and excludes the `linuxio` and `x86` discovery components before `hwloc_topology_load()` so hwloc only discovers the NUMA node and CPU sets that TSL uses.

head_commit.message:
Upgrade XLA's Bazel `@hwloc` dependency from 2.7.1 to 2.13.0.

XLA's Bazel workspace (`hwloc/workspace.bzl`) was pinned to `hwloc 2.7.1` (from 2022), missing years of upstream topology fixes and performance improvements. In particular, `hwloc 2.7.1` reads Linux `/sys` topology files via stdio `fopen`/`fgets`/`fclose` (allocating and freeing a heap buffer per file during `hwloc_topology_load`), whereas `hwloc 2.13.0` uses stack-buffered `openat`/`read`/`close` (`hwloc_read_path_by_length`), significantly reducing syscall and allocator overhead during NUMA topology initialization.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Simplify and optimize CpuLayoutAssignment

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Simplify and optimize CpuLayoutAssignment

## Problem

`CpuLayoutAssignment` built temporary `Shape` and `std::vector` objects on
every operand to construct row major and column major layouts. Tuple shaped
`kAllGather` and `kReduceScatter` instructions also left operand layout
constraints unset, letting downstream users overwrite their mandatory major
dimension layouts.

## Approach

Replace `RowMajorShape` and `ColMajorShape` with `LayoutUtil` helpers that
clear preexisting layout fields and avoid heap allocations. Constrain both
tuple outputs and array operands on `kAllGather` and `kReduceScatter` before
assigning default layouts to remaining rank 2 or higher array operands. Skip
1D constants in `ShouldMakeOperandColumnMajor` because row major and column
major layouts are identical for rank at most 1 shapes.

Existing valid CPU programs keep the same assigned layouts. Tuple collectives
and inputs with preexisting tiles or split configs now receive clean host
layouts. No flags are added.

## Tests

- `//xla/service/cpu:cpu_layout_assignment_test` pins tile and split config
  stripping, 1D constant dots, and array and variadic `all-gather` and
  `reduce-scatter` layouts.

Replace `RowMajorShape` and `ColMajorShape` with `LayoutUtil` helpers that
clear preexisting layout fields and avoid heap allocations. Constrain both
tuple outputs and array operands on `kAllGather` and `kReduceScatter` before
assigning default layouts to remaining rank 2 or higher array operands. Skip
1D constants in `ShouldMakeOperandColumnMajor` because row major and column
major layouts are identical for rank at most 1 shapes.

Existing valid CPU programs keep the same assigned layouts. Tuple collectives
and inputs with preexisting tiles or split configs now receive clean host
layouts. No flags are added.

- `//xla/service/cpu:cpu_layout_assignment_test` pins tile and split config

display_title: Fix C++20, libc++, and CUDA 13.4.1 compatibility issues in XLA.

head_commit.message:
Fix C++20, libc++, and CUDA 13.4.1 compatibility issues in XLA.

Preparing XLA for upcoming C++20, LLVM `libc++`, and CUDA 13.4.1 toolchain upgrades surfaces three build and test issues:

1. In C++20 mode, `ABSL_CONST_INIT` expands to `constinit`, which requires `constinit` on both `extern` declarations and initializing definitions. Because `xla_op_utils.h` declares the `kHloSparseCoreV0*` string constants with `TF_CONST_INIT extern const`, defining them as `constexpr` in `oss/xla_op_utils.cc` triggers `-Wmissing-constinit`. Update the OSS definitions to `TF_CONST_INIT const` to match `google/xla_op_utils.cc`.
2. Unlike `libstdc++`, `libc++` annotates `std::mutex` with Clang thread-safety attributes (`capability("mutex")`). In `EngineHeuristicsBuilder_v8::build()`, `cudnn-frontend` conditionally locks and unlocks `get_heur_b_mutex()` across two separate `if (m_heuristics.mode == CUDNN_HEUR_MODE_B)` blocks around `detail::finalize(...)`, triggering `-Wthread-safety-analysis`. Replace the split `.lock()` and `.unlock()` calls with a scoped `std::lock_guard<std::mutex>`.
3. In CUDA 13.4.1, `nvJitLinkComplete()` can return `NVJITLINK_SUCCESS` even when `nvJitLinkGetErrorLog()` contains `ptxas` register spill diagnostics. Always fetch `nvJitLinkGetErrorLog()` and validate it with `CreateErrorFromPTXASLog()` before checking `linking_result`.

display_title: Switch from libstdc++ to statically linked libc++

head_commit.message:
Switch from libstdc++ to statically linked libc++

This update enables building and testing Tensorflow with statically linked libc++ (LLVM 22) on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), adds C++20 support, and introduces Manylinux 2.27 compatible wheels.

Patches:
third_party/tensorflow/third_party/tf_runtime/invoke_result.patch
Replaces std::result_of_t (removed in C++20 libc++) with std::invoke_result_t in @tf_runtime, which is pinned to an external GitHub commit in OSS builds.

third_party/xla/third_party/mkl_dnn/eltwise_injector_lower_bound.patch
Why needed: Replaces entry_map_.find(key) on std::multimap with entry_map_.lower_bound(key) in @onednn_async (v3.12.3), @onednn_async_aarch64, and @mkl_dnn_acl_compatible (v3.11.3) so eltwise_injector iterates over all matching entries under C++20 libc++ (fixing the segfault in //tensorflow/core/kernels/mkl:mkl_fused_ops_test).

third_party/tensorflow/third_party/com_google_highway/build.patch
Why needed: Updates hunk context lines for the com_google_highway bump from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0.

Other changes
third_party/tensorflow/core/kernels/cwise_ops.h
In libc++, std::function has a different size and alignment on the x86_64 host (sizeof = 48, alignof = 16 due to 16-byte long double alignment in std::aligned_storage) than on the NVPTX64 CUDA device (sizeof = 32, alignof = 8). Because the comparison functors in cwise_ops.h inherited from std::function<bool(T, T)> and are embedded by value inside Eigen::TensorEvaluator CUDA kernel arguments, this host/device layout mismatch shifted the offsets of the GPU tensor pointers in the kernel parameter buffer and caused CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS crashes. Replacing : std::function<bool(T, T)> with using result_type = bool; keeps the typedef required by Eigen while making the functors stateless 1-byte structs with identical layout on host and device.

third_party/tensorflow/core/util/gpu_device_functions.h
In CUDA device code, Eigen::half (__half) and Eigen::bfloat16 (__nv_bfloat16) have explicit Eigen::numext::bit_cast specializations to and from uint16_t (using CUDA intrinsics like __half_as_ushort and __ushort_as_bfloat16), but no direct specialization between Eigen::half and Eigen::bfloat16. Without a direct specialization, Eigen::numext::bit_cast<Eigen::bfloat16>(Eigen::half) falls back to memcpy between two different class types in device registers, which NVCC's device compiler (cicc) optimizes into 0—causing GpuAtomicAdd on bfloat16 (e.g., in gather_op_test_gpu) to produce all zeros. Routing the conversion through uint16_t in detail::GpuAtomicCasHelper uses the explicit CUDA intrinsic specializations instead of the broken memcpy fallback.

head_commit.message:
Add AOT compatibility goldens for single-GPU library thunks

The XLA:GPU AOT compatibility tests only covered collective and control-flow
thunks, so a serialization break in a library or custom-call thunk went
unnoticed. This adds more tests, one single-GPU target per thunk, each with one minimal HLO op: `triangular_solve_aot_test`,
`fft_aot_test`, `convolution_aot_test`, `cublas_lt_matmul_aot_test`,
`ffi_custom_call_aot_test` and `rng_seed_aot_test`.

Each thunk depends on a different library or emitter, and golden versions are
per target, so one target per thunk keeps a library change (e.g. a cuBLAS
version bump) from creating new golden versions for unrelated thunks.

The cuBLASLt heuristic picks different algorithms on machines of the same arch
(algo_id 16 or 23 on B200), so `cublas_lt_matmul_aot_test` pins the algorithm
per arch and requires the runtime to rebuild it exactly. Its golden then does
not depend on the test machine, and a runtime that can no longer rebuild an
older algorithm fails the test instead of falling back to the heuristic.

The GPU test parameter helpers move from `collective_aot_test_base` into
`gpu_aot_test_params`, because the single-GPU targets have no collectives.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Unify one-hot-to-gather lowering and support batched one-hot dots and masked sum reductions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Unify one-hot-to-gather lowering and support batched one-hot dots and masked sum reductions.

One-hot selections contracted along a dimension of size `K` appear in XLA:GPU HLO in two forms:
1. As `kDot` instructions where one operand is a one-hot mask `convert(compare(broadcast(indices), iota, EQ))` (with or without batch dimensions).
2. Directly as standalone 1-D masked sum reductions `reduce_sum(select(compare(broadcast(indices), iota(reduce_dim), EQ), on_true, broadcast(0)), 0)` emitted by frontends as elementwise `compare` + `convert`/`select` + `reduce_sum` without going through `kDot`.

Evaluating either pattern as an `O(K)` contraction or reduction scans all `K` elements per output position and, when fused into a consumer reduction kernel (such as a Triton normalization kernel), forces every consumer CTA to re-read and reduce the `K`-wide operand along the contracted dimension. Previously, `DotStrengthReduction` only rewrote unbatched one-hot `kDot` instructions, and standalone one-hot `reduce_sum` patterns were not simplified to gathers.

This change:
1. display_title: Add AOT compatibility goldens for single-GPU library thunks

head_commit.message:
Add AOT compatibility goldens for single-GPU library thunks

The XLA:GPU AOT compatibility tests only covered collective and control-flow
thunks, so a serialization break in a library or custom-call thunk went
unnoticed. This adds one single-GPU target per thunk, each with one minimal HLO
op: `triangular_solve_aot_test` (TriangularSolve inside Sequential),
`fft_aot_test`, `convolution_aot_test`, `cublas_lt_matmul_aot_test`,
`ffi_custom_call_aot_test` (RAFT TopK) and `rng_seed_aot_test`.

Each thunk depends on a different library or emitter, and golden versions are
per target, so one target per thunk keeps a library change (e.g. a cuBLAS
version bump) from creating new golden versions for unrelated thunks.

The cuBLASLt heuristic picks different algorithms on machines of the same arch
(algo_id 16 or 23 on B200), so `cublas_lt_matmul_aot_test` pins the algorithm
per arch and requires the runtime to rebuild it exactly. Its golden then does
not depend on the test machine, and a runtime that can no longer rebuild an
older algorithm fails the test instead of falling back to the heuristic.

The GPU test parameter helpers move from `collective_aot_test_base` into
`gpu_aot_test_params`, because the single-GPU targets have no collectives.

CuDnn is left out: the serialized cuDNN graph embeds the cuDNN frontend's
process-wide graph id, so its golden would depend on test order.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Linearize small staged async H2D transfers inline in CommonPjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Linearize small staged async H2D transfers inline in CommonPjRtClient.

When `CommonPjRtClient::LinearizeIntoImpl` stages an asynchronous
host-to-device transfer (`HostBufferSemantics::kImmutableUntilTransferCompletes`),
dispatching small buffers through `async_work_runner()->ExecuteWhenReady(...)`
adds an extra thread-pool hop per tensor even when host staging capacity is
immediately available, exposing multi-host synchronous steps to work-queue
tail latency.

In `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client.cc`, linearize non-empty buffers up to 512 KiB
(`kMaxInlineAsyncLinearizeBytes`) and initiate `CopyRawHostToDeviceAndReturnEvent`
inline on the caller thread when the allocated `PjRtStagingBuffer` `AsyncValue`
is already available without error, while preserving async error-event and
`on_done_with_host_buffer` callback semantics if `Linearize` fails and
continuing to schedule larger or throttled transfers on `async_work_runner()`.

On a 256-chip (64-host, 4 chips/host) TPU training workload transferring 8
small tiled input tensors (264 KiB total per chip) each step, eliminating
redundant async thread hops on ready host-to-device transfers removed
25–118s single-straggler H2D tail-latency stalls (25s+ stalls dropped from 11
in 4,200 steps [max 118.0s] to 0 in 3,761 steps) and increased steady-state
throughput from 100.6–106.3 steps/min to 138.2–157.9 steps/min (+30%–43%).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010860094

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Restrict hwloc topology discovery in `numa_hwloc.cc` to NUMA and CPU objects.

head_commit.message:
Restrict hwloc topology discovery in `numa_hwloc.cc` to NUMA and CPU objects.

By default, `GetHWLocTopology()` in `numa_hwloc.cc` loads the full machine hardware hierarchy—including CPU cache levels, PCI/OS I/O devices (`linuxio`), and per-core `x86` CPUID probing—even though TSL's NUMA utilities only ever query `HWLOC_OBJ_NUMANODE` and CPU affinity sets. On large multi-socket / high-core-count hosts, this redundant discovery adds unnecessary sysfs traversal and CPUID probing overhead during NUMA initialization. This change configures `HWLOC_TYPE_FILTER_KEEP_NONE` and excludes the `linuxio` and `x86` discovery components before `hwloc_topology_load()` so hwloc only discovers the NUMA node and CPU sets that TSL uses.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010609292

XLA's Bazel workspace (`hwloc/workspace.bzl`) was pinned to `hwloc 2.7.1` (from 2022), missing years of upstream topology fixes and performance improvements. name: CI ROCm
display_title: Fix stack buffer overflow in CudaStream IsFabricMemory.

head_commit.message:
Fix stack buffer overflow in CudaStream IsFabricMemory.

`cuPointerGetAttribute` with `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ALLOWED_HANDLE_TYPES` writes a 64-bit bitmask (`uint64_t`) to the output pointer. Passing a 4-byte `unsigned int` in `IsFabricMemory` overflows 4 bytes onto the stack, corrupting adjacent stack slots (such as callee-saved `%rbx` when compiled with `-Os`) and causing a `SIGSEGV` in `CudaStream::Memcpy`.

Change `handle_types` in `IsFabricMemory` from `unsigned int` to `uint64_t` to match the 8-byte write performed by the CUDA driver.

head_commit.message:
PR #51881: [XLA:GPU] Fix data race constructing incarnation maps.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51881

📝 Summary of Changes

With >1 GPU per process, the per-GPU launcher threads raced to build + save an incarnation map in a shared per-process options structure. This could lead to heap corruption and deadlocks. This change saves the map made by each thread to a local copy of the options to avoid the race.

🎯 Justification

Fixes flaky deadlocks/crashes in JAX test `//tests/multiprocess:multihost_utils_test_gpu`.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

n/a

Added a test that hits the relevant codepath, although the check that makes it reliably fail before this PR is a bit unsatisfactory (it just checks the shared options do not have a map saved after execution). It should fail reliably under TSAN before the fix.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add a pass to convert an emitted kernel into a callable function.

Add the `VirtualizeSubKernelPass` MLIR pass that operates on `llvm` + `nvvm` modules. The pass:
1. Strips trailing scratch pointer arguments from Triton modules.
2. Appends `rel_bid_i32` to the entry signature.
3. Virtualizes `ctaid.{x,y,z}`, `nctaid.{x,y,z}`, `tid.{x,y,z}`, and `ntid.{x,y,z}` (delinearizing 2D/3D grids and thread blocks).

5. Packs shared memory globals into 16-byte-aligned byte offsets of external `@global_smem` and records "xla.shared_memory_bytes" attribute.

display_title: Fix stack buffer overflow in CudaStream IsFabricMemory.

head_commit.message:
Fix stack buffer overflow in CudaStream IsFabricMemory.

`cuPointerGetAttribute` with `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ALLOWED_HANDLE_TYPES` writes a 64-bit bitmask (`uint64_t`) to the output pointer. Passing a 4-byte `unsigned int` in `IsFabricMemory` overflows 4 bytes onto the stack, corrupting adjacent stack slots (such as callee-saved `%rbx` when compiled with `-Os`) and causing a `SIGSEGV` in `CudaStream::Memcpy`.

Change `handle_types` in `IsFabricMemory` from `unsigned int` to `uint64_t` to match the 8-byte write performed by the CUDA driver.

display_title: Switch from libstdc++ to statically linked libc++

head_commit.message:
Switch from libstdc++ to statically linked libc++

This update enables building and testing Tensorflow with statically linked libc++ (LLVM 22) on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), adds C++20 support, and introduces Manylinux 2.27 compatible wheels.

Patches:
third_party/tensorflow/third_party/tf_runtime/invoke_result.patch
Replaces std::result_of_t (removed in C++20 libc++) with std::invoke_result_t in @tf_runtime, which is pinned to an external GitHub commit in OSS builds.

third_party/xla/third_party/mkl_dnn/eltwise_injector_lower_bound.patch
Why needed: Replaces entry_map_.find(key) on std::multimap with entry_map_.lower_bound(key) in @onednn_async (v3.12.3), @onednn_async_aarch64, and @mkl_dnn_acl_compatible (v3.11.3) so eltwise_injector iterates over all matching entries under C++20 libc++ (fixing the segfault in //tensorflow/core/kernels/mkl:mkl_fused_ops_test).

third_party/tensorflow/third_party/com_google_highway/build.patch
Why needed: Updates hunk context lines for the com_google_highway bump from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0.

Other changes
third_party/tensorflow/core/kernels/cwise_ops.h
In libc++, std::function has a different size and alignment on the x86_64 host (sizeof = 48, alignof = 16 due to 16-byte long double alignment in std::aligned_storage) than on the NVPTX64 CUDA device (sizeof = 32, alignof = 8). Because the comparison functors in cwise_ops.h inherited from std::function<bool(T, T)> and are embedded by value inside Eigen::TensorEvaluator CUDA kernel arguments, this host/device layout mismatch shifted the offsets of the GPU tensor pointers in the kernel parameter buffer and caused CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS crashes. Replacing : std::function<bool(T, T)> with using result_type = bool; keeps the typedef required by Eigen while making the functors stateless 1-byte structs with identical layout on host and device.

third_party/tensorflow/core/util/gpu_device_functions.h
In CUDA device code, Eigen::half (__half) and Eigen::bfloat16 (__nv_bfloat16) have explicit Eigen::numext::bit_cast specializations to and from uint16_t (using CUDA intrinsics like __half_as_ushort and __ushort_as_bfloat16), but no direct specialization between Eigen::half and Eigen::bfloat16. Without a direct specialization, Eigen::numext::bit_cast<Eigen::bfloat16>(Eigen::half) falls back to memcpy between two different class types in device registers, which NVCC's device compiler (cicc) optimizes into 0—causing GpuAtomicAdd on bfloat16 (e.g., in gather_op_test_gpu) to produce all zeros. Routing the conversion through uint16_t in detail::GpuAtomicCasHelper uses the explicit CUDA intrinsic specializations instead of the broken memcpy fallback.

display_title: Add 2D `group_size` swizzling and storage-aware Triton search

head_commit.message:
Add 2D `group_size` swizzling and storage-aware Triton search

Linear row-major CTA launch order thrashes the L2 cache on large and batched
GEMMs, while `TritonDotFusionSearchSpace` currently prices narrow or sub-byte
operands at their expanded compute bitwidth (filtering out valid 4-stage WGMMA
TMA configs on Hopper).

We schedule batch dimensions outermost and swap `M`/`N` majorness when the LHS
parallel dimension is smaller on large dots in
`GetParallelDimensionsPermutation`, and remap 2D CTA tile IDs into
`group_size`-wide blocks in `ApplyDotGroupSizeTileIdRemapping` (using a
constant tail group width so partial tail groups avoid dynamic integer
division in PTX). `ConvertTritonGemmConfig` predicts root output tiles
directly and enables `group_size = 8` on large grids whose operand footprint
exceeds the L2 cache.

In `TritonDotFusionSearchSpace`, we track physical operand storage bitwidths
for shared memory stages and large-GEMM arithmetic intensity floors, enforce
Hopper WGMMA 256-bit contracting atoms and 4-to-16 warp bounds, and prune
configs that exceed device accumulator register budgets.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add L2-flushed TMA bulk write kernel for GPU bandwidth benchmarking.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add L2-flushed TMA bulk write kernel for GPU bandwidth benchmarking.

Standard device-to-device memcpy saturates HBM differently from Hopper tensor memory accelerator (TMA) bulk asynchronous writes and benefits from residual L2 cache residency on smaller transfers, so it cannot reproduce the HBM bandwidth derate tables used by the GPU dot fusion cost model, which were measured with the `write_ublkcp` kernel of NVIDIA's `nv_stream` benchmark.

Introduce `MeasureWriteUblkcpBandwidthBytesPerSec(ordinal, dma_size_bytes)`, which measures cold-L2 bulk write bandwidth in bytes per second for one transfer size (a multiple of 16 bytes, as `cp.async.bulk` requires). The kernel writes one 4 KiB tile per 256-thread block with `cp.async.bulk.global.shared::cta`. Before every timed launch a scratch buffer the size of the H100 L2 cache is written and freed, which makes the driver flush the cache; the fastest of 16 such launches is reported, which rejects host-side launch jitter the same way the reference benchmark's best-of-configurations search does. Devices older than compute capability 9.0 are rejected with `kUnimplemented`. The function leaves `ordinal` as the calling thread's current CUDA device: switching back was measured to add ~1 µs of launch latency to every later launch and to skew transfers below 8 MiB by 10-15%.

The library gets its own test target that runs on both `a100` and `h100`, so the measurement path and the pre-Hopper `kUnimplemented` rejection are both exercised, and the existing `gpu_bandwidth_benchmark_test` (which also runs on AMD GPUs) stays untouched.

The CUDA kernel is compiled into `:gpu_bandwidth_kernels_cuda`; the public `:gpu_bandwidth_kernels` target selects it with `if_cuda_is_configured` and otherwise links `gpu_bandwidth_kernels_stub.cc`, which returns `kUnimplemented`, so portable callers can include the header without an `#if GOOGLE_CUDA` guard.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Don't use AMD TDM for tiles with out-of-bounds singleton offsets.

AMD TDM folds singleton (size-1) tile dimension offsets into the base pointer
and drops those dimensions from the tensor descriptor, bypassing hardware bounds
checks when tile propagation (e.g. through `pad`) produces out-of-bounds
offsets. Decline TDM unless singleton offsets are provably in bounds, and
document the out-of-bounds semantics of `xtile.extract` and `xtile.insert`.

head_commit.message:
Cancel and drain the Profile RPC when Terminate fails.

When the `Terminate` RPC failed, `SubprocessProfilingSession::Stop()` returned right away. The cleanup cancelled the async `Profile` call, but nothing read its completion from `completion_queue_`, so the call leaked (ASan reports it). `Stop()` now cancels the `Profile` call when `Terminate` fails, waits for it on the completion queue, and then returns the `Terminate` error.

display_title: Fix stack buffer overflow in CudaStream IsFabricMemory.

head_commit.message:
Fix stack buffer overflow in CudaStream IsFabricMemory.

`cuPointerGetAttribute` with `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ALLOWED_HANDLE_TYPES` writes a 64-bit bitmask (`uint64_t`) to the output pointer. Passing a 4-byte `unsigned int` in `IsFabricMemory` overflows 4 bytes onto the stack, corrupting adjacent stack slots (such as callee-saved `%rbx` when compiled with `-Os`) and causing a `SIGSEGV` in `CudaStream::Memcpy`.

Change `handle_types` in `IsFabricMemory` from `unsigned int` to `uint64_t` to match the 8-byte write performed by the CUDA driver.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010638798

display_title: [XLA] Add BackendConfigWrapper::content_id()

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add BackendConfigWrapper::content_id()

Backends derive values from backend configs on hot paths, and custom calls that
embed a kernel carry configs of several megabytes. A cache of derived values
must notice when a config changes. The address of the wrapper cannot tell,
because ApplyFnOnProto mutates the wrapper in place.
BackendConfigWrapper::content_id() returns an id of the current contents that
changes whenever they change, and ids are never reused.
HloInstruction::backend_config_content_id() exposes it, so backends can key
caches of derived values by it.

display_title: PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

head_commit.message:
PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48875

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`AlgebraicSimplifier` rewrites a `reduce-window` with a 1x...x1 window (no stride, dilation or reversal, add/min/max reducer) into a plain elementwise op on the operand, wrapped in a `pad` when the window has padding. The wrapper was only built when some padding amount was positive. Window padding can also be negative (a crop), which changes the shape just like positive padding does. With only negative padding the rewrite replaced a `f32[7,4]` reduce-window with a `f32[8,4]` add, `ReplaceInstruction` failed its shape RET_CHECK, and the simplifier turned that into a fatal CHECK, so compilation aborted the process.

This change applies the positive padding amounts with a `pad` and the negative amounts with a `slice`, so the replacement always has the reduce-window's shape. It deliberately never emits a `pad` with negative edge padding: such a pad would be seen by consumers later in the same simplifier sweep, and the pad-into-reduce-window / pad-into-convolution folds in this file assume non-negative edge padding, so a crop feeding a padded reduce-window would have been folded into a wrong net padding (#48715 covers that fold). The mixed-sign case, which previously produced a negative pad and relied on `HandlePad` to turn it into a slice, now takes the same pad-plus-slice path. For the module from the issue the whole thing simplifies to `slice(x)`.

Tests added to `algebraic_simplifier_test.cc`: `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePad` (aborts the test binary before this change), `TrivialReduceWindowWithMixedSignPad`, and `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePadFeedingPaddedReduceWindow` (checks the consumer keeps its own padding).

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #48719. Compile-time process abort on valid HLO (negative reduce-window padding is documented and reachable from `lax.reduce_window`). The pass is shared by all backends.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test`

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None added (pass-level fix). Verified locally on CPU that the issue's module and the crop-feeding-a-padded-reduce-window module compile and produce the expected values.
Copybara import of the project:

--
9084afa58b0af7090de1af90957c62ea4bfd8926 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

[XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

The AlgebraicSimplifier rewrite of a reduce-window with a 1x...x1 window
into an elementwise op only padded the result when some window padding
amount was positive. Negative window padding (a crop) also changes the
shape, so a window with only negative padding produced a replacement of
the wrong shape and ReplaceInstruction CHECK-failed, aborting compilation.

Apply positive padding amounts with a pad and negative amounts with a
slice. The rewrite no longer emits pads with negative edge padding, which
the pad-into-reduce-window and pad-into-convolution folds do not handle.

Fixes #48719.

--
8e49526621a668880fc6c37e7e5783b77a538fa6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Emit the crop slice before the pad in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

Create the slice for the negative window padding directly on the
elementwise op and put the pad for the positive padding on top of it, so
that slice-sinking passes can move the slice into the elementwise op.

--
bbda2f1733814d3a64a57f18371852a3c1eb1da6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Handle window padding that crops beyond the dimension in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

A negative padding larger than the dimension (e.g. f32[2] with pad=-3_2)
is valid HLO as long as the output size stays non-negative, but the slice
emitted for the crop then has start > limit and the simplifier fails.
No operand element reaches the output in that case, so replace the
reduce-window with a broadcast of the init value instead.

Merging this change closes #48875

head_commit.message:
Fix custom-op shim compatibility and USE_PYWRAP_RULES parsing in TensorFlow.

Downstream custom-op libraries (such as TF.Text) that compile `tf_op_shim` sources directly against TensorFlow wheel headers and link dynamically against `libtensorflow_framework.so` need the shim source files exported and must avoid direct protobuf `Map::at()` lookups across the shared-library boundary. - Export `shape.cc`, `tf_op_shim.cc`, and `tf_tensor_view.cc` in `tensorflow/lite/kernels/shim/BUILD`.
- Look up op attributes via `::tensorflow::AttrSlice(context_->def()).Find(attr_name)` in `TfInitContext::GetAttr` and remove an unused `error_codes.proto.h` include.
- Parse `USE_PYWRAP_RULES` in `python_version.bzl` and `python_repo.bzl.oss` using `.get("USE_PYWRAP_RULES", "").lower() in ("true", "1")`.

display_title: Fix USE_PYWRAP_RULES parsing and missing TSL header exports.

head_commit.message:
Fix USE_PYWRAP_RULES parsing and missing TSL header exports.

In `python_version.bzl`, `bool(os.environ.get("USE_PYWRAP_RULES", False))` evaluates non-empty strings such as `"0"` or `"false"` to `True`, preventing `USE_PYWRAP_RULES` from being disabled via environment variable. Additionally, TSL's legacy monitoring header filegroups and `tf_additional_lib_deps()` are missing header targets needed when compiling against exported header sets.

- Parse `USE_PYWRAP_RULES` in `python_version.bzl` using `.get("USE_PYWRAP_RULES", "").lower() in ("true", "1")`.
- Add `counter_gauge.h` and `label_array_utils.h` to the `mobile_hdrs_only_runtime`, `legacy_lib_monitoring_lib_headers`, and `legacy_lib_monitoring_all_headers` filegroups in `xla/tsl/lib/monitoring/BUILD`.
- Add `@com_google_absl//absl/status:status_macros`, `//tsl/platform:protobuf`, and `//xla/tsl/concurrency:executor` to `tf_additional_lib_deps()`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Allow clearing scheduling group annotations on non-async instructions.

head_commit.message:
Allow clearing scheduling group annotations on non-async instructions.

When XLA cannot schedule every instruction in a `_scheduling_group_id` group at once (for example, when an in-order async queue adds a dependency on another in-flight operation during scheduling), `DefaultSchedulerCore::ScheduleAnnotation` clears the group annotation on the remaining unscheduled instructions so they can be scheduled normally later.

Previously, `ScheduleAnnotation` asserted that any remaining unscheduled instruction in the group was an `async-start` or `async-done`. However, `LegalizeSchedulingAnnotations` can propagate a group ID onto intermediate non-async instructions (such as a `bitcast` between two dependent collectives in the same group). When the downstream collective start is deferred, those upstream non-async instructions also remain unscheduled and hit the `RET_CHECK` failure.

Remove the async-only `RET_CHECK` when clearing annotations on unscheduled instructions in `ScheduleAnnotation`, and add a unit test in `xla/service/latency_hiding_scheduler_test.cc` covering a propagated `bitcast` inside a partially scheduled group.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010617365

display_title: [Pallas:TPU] Zero-extend 16-bit top_k indices to int32

head_commit.message:
[Pallas:TPU] Zero-extend 16-bit top_k indices to int32

In `_top_k_impl`, `lax.argmax` on `bfloat16` inputs returns 16-bit indices, and
the reduced dimension may have up to 2^16 elements, so the indices are unsigned.
Cast via `uint16` before widening to `int32` so the conversion lowers to
`arith.extui` instead of `arith.extsi`, which previously sign-extended indices >= 32768 into negative values.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

Adds StreamExecutor::CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocator, which returns a
MemoryAllocator whose physical memory is placed on one locality domain (die)
of the device. The CUDA implementation creates the physical memory with
cuMemCreate, using location type CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN
(CUDA 13.4 and newer). It rejects out-of-range domain ids, older CUDA
versions, and the cuMemAlloc path (use_vmm=false), and never falls back to
whole-device memory.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Preserve narrow-float values across identity reduce-precision in XLA.

head_commit.message:
Preserve narrow-float values across identity reduce-precision in XLA.

`jax.checkpoint` (remat) pins saved floating-point residuals that are also read in the forward pass with `reduce-precision` set to the element type's own exponent and mantissa bit widths so that excess-precision optimizations cannot give the forward and backward passes different values. For 8-bit and 4-bit floating-point types, `FloatNormalization` previously promoted an identity `reduce-precision` to a wider floating-point type (`f16` or `f32`), turning it into a non-identity IEEE-style bit-fiddle with infinities and without subnormals (for example, corrupting `f8e4m3fn` values in 256..448 to `NaN` and flushing subnormals to zero). `HloEvaluator` and the MLIR and LLVM emitters had the same issue when lowering identity `reduce-precision` ops.

Add `primitive_util::HasFloatingPointPrecision` and treat `reduce-precision` instructions whose `exponent_bits` and `mantissa_bits` match their element type's bit widths as supported in low precision in `FloatSupport`, without allowing `--xla_allow_excess_precision` to elide the low-precision conversion feeding them. Short-circuit identity `reduce-precision` in `HloEvaluator`, `EmitReducePrecisionIR` (also replacing `nbits - 1 - src_mantissa_bits` with `primitive_util::ExponentWidth(src_ty)` because `F8E8M0FNU` has no sign bit), and `mapMhloOpToStdScalarOp` (fixing the off-by-one in `HasDefaultMantissaBits` and `HasDefaultExponentBits`, where `mlir::FloatType::getFPMantissaWidth()` includes the implicit leading bit and unsigned float types such as `Float8E8M0FNUType` have no sign bit via `llvm::APFloat::semanticsHasSignedRepr`).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1009850192

only single-input reductions worked, so argmax-style fusions
could not use the TensorIR backend.
