display_title: Switch from libstdc++ to statically linked libc++

head_commit.message:
Switch from libstdc++ to statically linked libc++

This update enables building and testing Tensorflow with statically linked libc++ (LLVM 22) on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), adds C++20 support, and introduces Manylinux 2.27 compatible wheels.

Patches:
third_party/tensorflow/third_party/tf_runtime/invoke_result.patch
Replaces std::result_of_t (removed in C++20 libc++) with std::invoke_result_t in @tf_runtime, which is pinned to an external GitHub commit in OSS builds.

third_party/xla/third_party/mkl_dnn/eltwise_injector_lower_bound.patch
Why needed: Replaces entry_map_.find(key) on std::multimap with entry_map_.lower_bound(key) in @onednn_async (v3.12.3), @onednn_async_aarch64, and @mkl_dnn_acl_compatible (v3.11.3) so eltwise_injector iterates over all matching entries under C++20 libc++ (fixing the segfault in //tensorflow/core/kernels/mkl:mkl_fused_ops_test).

third_party/tensorflow/third_party/com_google_highway/build.patch
Why needed: Updates hunk context lines for the com_google_highway bump from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0.

Other changes
third_party/tensorflow/core/kernels/cwise_ops.h
In libc++, std::function has a different size and alignment on the x86_64 host (sizeof = 48, alignof = 16 due to 16-byte long double alignment in std::aligned_storage) than on the NVPTX64 CUDA device (sizeof = 32, alignof = 8). Because the comparison functors in cwise_ops.h inherited from std::function<bool(T, T)> and are embedded by value inside Eigen::TensorEvaluator CUDA kernel arguments, this host/device layout mismatch shifted the offsets of the GPU tensor pointers in the kernel parameter buffer and caused CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS crashes. Replacing : std::function<bool(T, T)> with using result_type = bool; keeps the typedef required by Eigen while making the functors stateless 1-byte structs with identical layout on host and device.

third_party/tensorflow/core/util/gpu_device_functions.h
In CUDA device code, Eigen::half (__half) and Eigen::bfloat16 (__nv_bfloat16) have explicit Eigen::numext::bit_cast specializations to and from uint16_t (using CUDA intrinsics like __half_as_ushort and __ushort_as_bfloat16), but no direct specialization between Eigen::half and Eigen::bfloat16. Without a direct specialization, Eigen::numext::bit_cast<Eigen::bfloat16>(Eigen::half) falls back to memcpy between two different class types in device registers, which NVCC's device compiler (cicc) optimizes into 0—causing GpuAtomicAdd on bfloat16 (e.g., in gather_op_test_gpu) to produce all zeros. Routing the conversion through uint16_t in detail::GpuAtomicCasHelper uses the explicit CUDA intrinsic specializations instead of the broken memcpy fallback.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003532411

display_title: Allow clearing scheduling group annotations on non-async instructions.

head_commit.message:
Allow clearing scheduling group annotations on non-async instructions.

When XLA cannot schedule every instruction in a `_scheduling_group_id` group at once (for example, when an in-order async queue adds a dependency on another in-flight operation during scheduling), `DefaultSchedulerCore::ScheduleAnnotation` clears the group annotation on the remaining unscheduled instructions so they can be scheduled normally later.

Previously, `ScheduleAnnotation` asserted that any remaining unscheduled instruction in the group was an `async-start` or `async-done`. However, `LegalizeSchedulingAnnotations` can propagate a group ID onto intermediate non-async instructions (such as a `bitcast` between two dependent collectives in the same group). When the downstream collective start is deferred, those upstream non-async instructions also remain unscheduled and hit the `RET_CHECK` failure.

Remove the async-only `RET_CHECK` when clearing annotations on unscheduled instructions in `ScheduleAnnotation`, and add a unit test in `xla/service/latency_hiding_scheduler_test.cc` covering a propagated `bitcast` inside a partially scheduled group.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010561262

display_title: [XLA] Fix HLO parser crash when the wrapped op of a sugared async-start fails to parse

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix HLO parser crash when a sugared async-start's wrapped op fails to parse

CreateAsyncWrappedComputation returns nullptr when the wrapped instruction
of a sugared async-start (call-start, custom-call-start, ...) fails to
parse. The result was assigned into std::optional<HloComputation*>, which
engages the optional even for nullptr, so the following null check never
fired and the null computation reached HloInstruction::CreateAsyncStart,
where HloAsyncStartInstruction's constructor dereferenced it (SIGSEGV).
Keep the raw pointer in a local and return early when it is null, as the
code did before 8bc8533fb6.

Fixes #49227.

display_title: PR #50868: [XLA] Fix HLO parser crash when the wrapped op of a sugared async-start fails to parse

head_commit.message:
PR #50868: [XLA] Fix HLO parser crash when the wrapped op of a sugared async-start fails to parse

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50868

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Fixes #49227.

Parsing a sugared async start like `call-start(), to_apply={%nope}` segfaults instead of returning a parse error. `CreateAsyncWrappedComputation` returns a null `HloComputation*` when the wrapped instruction fails to parse, and that null gets assigned into `std::optional<HloComputation*> async_computation`. Assigning a pointer engages the optional, so the `if (!async_computation)` check never fires and the null computation reaches `HloInstruction::CreateAsyncStart`, where the `HloAsyncStartInstruction` constructor dereferences it.

This regressed in 8bc8533fb6 (the refactor that introduced `CreateAsyncWrappedComputation`); before that the code checked the raw root pointer. The fix keeps the result in a local pointer and returns early when it is null, same as before the refactor. Any sugared `*-start` op was affected, for example `custom-call-start()` without `custom_call_target` crashed the same way.

## 🎯 Justification

Malformed HLO text should produce an `INVALID_ARGUMENT` status, not kill the process. `run_hlo_module`, `hlo-opt` and every test that parses HLO go through this code.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

Two tests in `hlo_parser_test.cc`: `DesugarParsingTest_CallStart_InvalidToApply` (the input from the issue) and `DesugarParsingTest_CustomCallStart_MissingTarget` (different wrapped op, different failure). Both segfault at HEAD and pass with the fix.

```
bazel test //xla/hlo/parser:hlo_parser_test
```

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None needed, the change is in the parser error path only.
Copybara import of the project:

--

[XLA] Add BuildHloPassPipeline to build HloPassPipeline from proto.

Problem:    No driver turns HloPipelineProto into a runnable pipeline.
Solution:   Add BuildHloPassPipeline. It creates passes from HloPassRegistry.

A node with max_fixed_point_iterations > 1 is wrapped in HloPassFix. It keeps
the name and kind of that node, so it acts like HloPassFix<Pass> or
HloPassFix<HloPassPipeline>.
